SEARCH
Package neqsim.process.util.optimizer

Class ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.util.optimizer.ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator extends Object implements Serializable
Black-box evaluator for large multi-area ProcessModel optimization problems.

This evaluator fills the gap between the single-flowsheet ProcessSimulationEvaluator and integrated models composed of several named ProcessSystem areas. Decision variables are addressed with the existing ProcessAutomation syntax, for example "Wells::Producer A.flowRate". This keeps external optimizers independent of the internal Java object graph while still allowing objective and constraint functions to inspect the full model.

The intended use case is fixed-equipment throughput optimization: vary producer/feed rates, run the full ProcessModel, and stop when installed capacity constraints reveal the active bottleneck. Capacity constraints can be added explicitly to equipment or discovered through the EquipmentCapacityStrategyRegistry.

Version:
1.0
Author:
NeqSim Development Team

    • addBoundaryConstraint

      public ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator addBoundaryConstraint(String name, ProcessBoundaryConstraintEvidence.Metadata metadata, ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.BoundarySampleEvaluator sampleEvaluator, ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.ConstraintDefinition.Type type, double lowerBound, double upperBound, double equalityTolerance, String unit, boolean hard, double penaltyWeight, double residualScale)
      Adds a fully qualified process-boundary constraint.

      Bounds and units are frozen at registration. The structured sampler is invoked once after each completed model run; missing, non-finite, not-calculable, or out-of-validity evidence fails a hard constraint closed.

      Parameters:
      name - human-readable constraint name
      metadata - immutable boundary identity and provenance
      sampleEvaluator - structured runtime sampler
      type - lower, upper, range, or equality constraint
      lowerBound - lower bound or equality target
      upperBound - upper bound
      equalityTolerance - absolute equality tolerance
      unit - physical engineering unit
      hard - whether unavailable or violated evidence makes the point infeasible
      penaltyWeight - penalty multiplier
      residualScale - positive physical scale used for dimensionless violation only
      Returns:
      this evaluator for chaining

    • addEquipmentCapacityConstraints

      public ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator addEquipmentCapacityConstraints()
      Adds installed equipment capacity constraints from all process areas.

      Each enabled equipment capacity constraint becomes an upper-bound constraint where utilization must be less than or equal to 1.0. Constraint names are area-qualified as "area::equipment/constraint" so bottlenecks can be traced back to the full model.

      Returns:
      this evaluator for chaining

    • evaluate

      public ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.EvaluationResult evaluate(double[] parameterValues)
      Evaluates the process model at the supplied parameter values.

      Each registered objective and constraint callback is sampled exactly once after the model run. Raw and sign-adjusted objectives, and constraint values, margins, feasibility, and penalties, are derived from those same samples.

      Parameters:
      parameterValues - parameter vector with length equal to getParameterCount()
      Returns:
      complete evaluation result

    • selectActiveBottleneck

      private ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.BottleneckStatus selectActiveBottleneck(List<ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.BottleneckStatus> rankedCapacityConstraints)
      Selects the leading legacy-eligible bottleneck from a ranked snapshot.

      Preserve the historical findActiveBottleneck(ProcessModel) threshold: utilizations at or below -1.0, including negative infinity, are retained in the diagnostic ranking but are not exposed as the active bottleneck.

      Parameters:
      rankedCapacityConstraints - ranked capacity snapshots

    • rankCapacityConstraints

      public List<ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.BottleneckStatus> rankCapacityConstraints(ProcessModel model)
      Snapshots and ranks all enabled capacity constraints across the process model.

      Ranking is by descending utilization only. The sort is stable, so equal-utilization constraints preserve process area, equipment, and constraint registration order. Evidence confidence and applicability are retained as diagnostics but never change order or feasibility. Undefined (NaN) utilizations remain visible at the end of the ranking. Each dynamic value supplier is read exactly once.

      Parameters:
      model - process model in its current state
      Returns:
      immutable utilization-ranked constraint snapshots, or an empty list when the model is null or has no enabled capacity constraint

      Each dynamic supplier is invoked exactly once. The immutable returned rows separate normalized values from physical values and preserve deterministic area, equipment, and registration order for utilization ties.

    • estimateSensitivitiesWithQuality

      public ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.SensitivityQualityResult estimateSensitivitiesWithQuality(double[] parameterValues)
      Estimates an objective gradient and constraint-margin Jacobian with step-halving quality evidence.

      The configured finite-difference step is used as the coarse step and is halved once for the returned derivative. Objective and constraint sensitivities share the same base and perturbed process evaluations. Bounds determine the actual central, forward, backward, or fixed stencil independently for every parameter. The result records the actual steps, convergence, hard-constraint feasibility, evaluation errors, and scale-independent disagreement between the coarse and fine derivatives. Immutable parameter, selected-objective, and constraint snapshots bind every derivative column and row to the base-point engineering identity and units.

      Step-halving agreement only checks local numerical consistency. It does not establish differentiability across equipment/control regime changes and must not be interpreted as a Lagrange multiplier, shadow price, process-safety approval, or validity outside the sampled operating points.

      Parameters:
      parameterValues - parameter vector
      Returns:
      primary-objective gradient, constraint Jacobian, and immutable quality evidence
